rule.description: A package-level production function, method or type declared inside the repository module is reported when no supported entry point can reach it. Supported entry points are main functions, init functions, package-level var/const initializers and the exported API surface of public module packages (pkg/, pb/). Method dispatch through interfaces, external frameworks or reflection is conservatively treated as reachable, so a method is unreachable only when its receiver type is unreachable. Test files are not analyzed and a production declaration referenced only from tests stays unreachable.

checks.description: Apply one module-wide production reachability rule to every package-level function, method and type of the repository module and report each declaration no supported entry point can reach.
checks.detected_relation: supported module entry point -> production declaration with no reachable reference path
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: A production declaration that no supported entry point can reach is never executed at run time. Keeping it, together with the helper declarations it keeps referencing, preserves code paths that must be understood, reviewed and migrated while carrying no reachable behavior, which is the maintenance burden this dead_code_elimination case targets.

excluded.reason: Package-level constant declarations always evaluate at program startup, so the rule treats every var and const as a supported entry point and never reports them. This constant belongs to the injected digest-notification island and is intentionally left to the solver's cleanup responsibility rather than to checker detection, because a legit constant with the same shape could seed a live initializer.
